newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian shares end mostly lower as bank plummets.
newsitem.headline: Colombian shares end mostly lower as bank plummets.

text.p: Colombian shares ended mostly lower led by bank Bancoquia, which plummeted nearly 10 percent on market speculation about the possible collapse of its merger with Spain's Banco Santander.

Medellin's general price index shed 0.28 to end at 17,242.74 on volume of nearly 1.7 billion pesos. Bogota's lost 0.14 percent, closing at 1,118.85 on a volume of nearly 2 billion pesos. The owners of Bancoquia, Colombia's eighth largest in terms of assets, and financial arm of the Julio Mario Santo Domingo conglomerate, have announced plans to sell 51 percent of the bank to Banco Santander.

There was no news about the merger agreement Monday, but traders said the stock fell dramatically on fallout from Friday's announcement that Banco de Colombia had given up on efforts to form a strategic alliance with Spain's Banco Central Hispano-Americano.
"It seems that people linked the Banco de Colombia's frustrated negotiations with Spain's BCH with the talks with Santander, but there's no information to support that," said one Bogota-based broker.
However erroneous that linkage may be, Bancoquia fell 9.67 percent in Bogota to close at 2,800 pesos per share.

The bank's stock also fell sharply in Medellin, ending down 6.56 percent at 2,850 pesos a share. Banco de Colombia, which fell 1.25 percent Friday, extended it losses Monday. It ended down just 0.75 percent in Bogota at 392 pesos per share. But it shed 3.54 percent in Medellin, ending way below its book value at just 381 per share.

Brewer Bavaria, flagship of the Santo Domingo group, also closed lower, ending down 0.70 percent in Medellin at 7,855 pesos a share. Gains included Banco Ganadero, which closed up 2.05 percent in Bogota at 347 pesos per share.
